newsitem.title: GERMANY: EMI urges those capable to join ERM2.
newsitem.headline: EMI urges those capable to join ERM2.

text.p: The European Monetary Institute on Friday urged European Union countries which were capable of joining a new European exchange rate mechanism to do so, even though membership will be voluntary.

In a report on the operating framework for the future European Central Bank published on Friday, the EMI made clear that the option not to join the new system should only really be used by those whose economies have not converged enough with those of the core EU states.
The so-called ERM2 will be set up at the start of European monetary union to group European currencies which do not make the grade to join the euro.

"Membership will be voluntary," the EMI said on the new mechanism. But it added, "Nevertheless, EU member states with a derogation can be expected to join the mechanism once they have achieved a satisfactory degree of economic convergence."
Reluctance of the part of Britain and Sweden to commit to joining such a mechanism has angered countries at Europe's core.
